scientific_question: Can a source-grounded typed clause grammar realize nonidentical Korean sentence orders without changing the source semantic frame or inventing new predicates, and reject clearly forbidden polarity/causal/ellipsis moves?

execution.machine_guarantee: Exact typed semantic record pointer reuse, preauthored constituent conservation and finite licensed ordering; exactly 2 paragraphs and 5 fact slots per document.

korean_constructions: Constituent order based on fixed finite phrase permutations; Korean finite predicates remain last.
Case/particle selection for nominative, accusative, topic, instrumental with NFC Hangul last-syllable coda and ㄹ instrumental exception.
Information-given topic requires explicit discourse state; contrastive topic requires an independently declared warrant.
'다만' connective licensed only by source result→unmeasured limitation edge; no asserted cause induced.
scientific_limitations: Original Korean segments were manually authored as a tiny closed-domain grammar, not learned by a model or independently verified by a linguist.
Structural hash equality does not prove natural-language truth conditional equivalence; topic and phrase order can shift pragmatic emphasis.
The created passages remain close to factual source wording, and 4 examples are insufficient to infer idiomatic stylistic advantage.
No LLM generation, no GAN weight training, no independent human naturalness ratings, no comparison against a capable generic baseline.
The prior 18-draft v0.1 human reader survey is RETIRED as unusable due to elementary source and prose failures.
